1. Introduction 
 
1.1 Tourism – an Engine of Economic Growth 
 
Given the potential of tourism as a vehicle for job creation, economic growth and  
development, Tourism has been recognized as an engine for economic growth. 
Globally, strong economic growth has generated millions of new travelers looking for  
exceptional travel experiences, be it business or leisure, domestic, regional or 
international, and this trend is expected to continue with sustained momentum. 
 
1.2 Incredible India Brand 
 
The Government launched ‘Incredible India’ campaign to tap into the vast tourism  
potential of the country in an organized manner. An integrated communication 
strategy aimed at promoting India as the preferred destination for the international  
traveller was formulated. The campaign highlighted various facets of Indian culture  
and history such as yog a, spirituality, festivals and monuments. The Incredible India  
campaign is one of the most successful campaigns that placed India on the world  
tourism map. 
 
1.3 Increasing International Recognition 
 
India's philosophy of 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' sees the world as one family. It gives 
India an unwavering belief in multilateralism. India’s traditions of non -violence and 
pluralism, diversity and tolerance, its yoga and Ayurveda, its Bollywood and classical  
dances, are all well known. There is an increasing international recognition of India’s 
cultural and civilizational heritage. The rise of Indian diaspora to top echelons of  
technology industry and other professions across the world has given a great 
recognition to India. 
 
1.4 India Tourism – Growing consistently but yet to realize full potential 
 
As a travel destination, few other nations can offer the diversity of products and  
experiences found in India. Before COVID -19 pandemic, International Tourist Arrivals 
in India have been consistently growing with 17. 91 million international tourist 
arrivals in 2019. India, however stands at 23rd rank in terms of  international arrivals 
and 12th rank in terms of foreign exchange earnings from tourism for year 2019. 
India is yet to realize its full potential as a tourist destination. 
1.5 Aatmanirbhar Bharat – Overseas Demand will be crucial for Growth of Tourism 
 
Challenged by COVID-19, India has come out with the resolve to become self -reliant. 
“Aatmanirbhar Bharat” is a call to become vocal for local. It rests on the five pillars of 

54  
economy, infrastructure, systems, demography and demand. India’s quest for self - 
reliance is about creating strong enterprises in India. Enterprises that can become  
global forces. Self -reliance is about generating empl oyment and empowering our  
people to come out and create solutions that can define the future of our country. 
 
A thriving tourism industry is of vital importance for India’s journey towards 5 Trillion  
Dollar Economy. With the mantra of ‘vocal for local’, India seeks to attain 
“Aatmanirbhar Bharat” by realizing its full potential as a tourism destination. 
Overseas demand for Indian tourism products will be crucial for “Aatmnirbhar 
Bharat” 
 
1.6 Need for Greater Synergy with Indian Missions for promotion of Tourism 
 
Tourism destinations, the world over, are competing with each other  to increase  
their share in the global market. It will further intensify in future when international  
travel resumes post COVID-19 pandemic. The countries will adopt aggressive 
marketing and promotional strategies in source markets. This involves generating  
widespread awareness and generating interest in their tourism destinations and 
products amongst the trade and consumers and further, converting that interest into  
actual footfalls. 
The Ministry of Tourism has 8 offices overseas viz. Beijing, Dubai, Frankfurt, London,  
New York, Paris, Singapore and Tokyo. These offices play a pro-active role in 
enhancing tourist arrivals by promoting India in the tourism generating markets 
overseas. The overseas offices undertake various promotional activities for 
positioning India as a tourism destination in major source markets vis a vis other  
competing destination. 
Indian Missions abroad have also been promoting India as tourism destination and  
post pa ndemic, a renewed  effort will be required to  position India as preferred  
tourism destination. There  is a need to  have a coordinated strategy and framework 
to synergize the efforts of Ministry of Tourism with Ministry of External Affairs and  
Indian Missions. 
1.7 Partnership with Indian Missions for Inbound Tourism 
 
In order to forge partnership with Indian Missions for Inbound Tourism and ensure  
effective implementation, a detailed framework has been evolved covering the 
vision and objectives, key strategic areas, key operational areas and governance of  
the institutional arrangement. 
2. Vision and Objectives 

55  
2.1 Vision 
 
To create a unified strategy and forge partnership  amongst Ministry of Tourism,  
Indian Missions and other relevant Stakeholders to  promote Inbound Tourism to  
India 
2.2 Objectives 
 
The key objectives of the Strategy are: 
 
(i) Position India as the most favoured tourist destination 
(ii) Create right perception about India as a tourism destination 
(iii) Promote India as a 365 days destination 
(iv) Promote specific themes, destinations and products of Indian Tourism 
(v) Strengthen India’s role in various multilateral and bilateral forums on Tourism 
 
3. Role of Indian Missions in promoting Inbound Tourism 
 
Indian Missions will take ownership to promote Inbound tourism to India in the host 
countries where India Tourism Offices are not located i.e. in countries other than  
USA, UK, Germany, Russia, Dubai, China, Singapore and Japan. Missions will assign  
dedicated Officers for promotion of tourism and designate poin ts of contact for the  
Ministry of Tourism and other tourism stakeholders. 
 
In countries where India Tourism Overseas offices are located, they would work in  
close coordination with the respective Missions to undertake various promotional  
activities. 
 
Indian Missions and India Overseas offices will execute a strategized, targeted 
approach tailored to each host country to promote Inbound tourism to India. 
 
4. Key Strategic Areas 
 
4.1 Inbound Tourism Strategy to be a holistic approach 
 
Inbound tourism strategy should not to be just a campaign, but part of a holistic  
approach to promote Inbound tourism. It is important to focus on providing a safe,  
seamless, connected and unique experience to the visitors. Bringing together 
business and government to define smart  targets will be critical to ensure that the  
entire industry can coalesce and be held accountable to ambitious targets and their  
achievement. 

56  
The digital arena has become  the new playground for  brands to promote their  
products, services a nd destinations and effective digital strategy should be in place  
to promote Inbound tourism. 
 
4.2 Country specific Strategic Plans 
 
The Ministry of Tourism in consultation with Ministry of External Affairs and other  
relevant Ministries and Industry Stakeholders will identify the top source markets  
including established as well as emerging markets. In addition, focus areas such as  
Buddhist markets will be identified. 
 
The Ministry of Tourism will accordingly prepare country specific multi-year 
strategic plans for marketing in these Key Markets, which should include 
 
(i) Needs, Requirements and Preference of travelers 
 
The Missions can help in identifying the needs and requirements of the 
travelers from these source  markets and their preferences such as  Cultural 
and Heritage, Yoga and Wellness, Adventure, Eco -tourism, Medical, MICE etc.  
Industry can also provide the feedback. 
 
(ii) Specific Initiatives and campaigns 
 
The plans may identify specific initiatives and campaigns apart from generic  
measures applicab le to all the markets. The plans may also have targets for  
specific markets. 
 
(iii) Mega familiarization tours 
 
Plans for organizing Mega familiarization tours for specific countries and 
covering specific tourism offerings such as Culture and Heritage, Yoga and  
Wellness, Medical Value travel, Adventure tourism need to be included in the  
Plans. 
 
(iv) International Roadshows 
 
Plans for Important International Roadshows should be prepared in 
consultation with Indian Missions and Industry Stakeholders for various 
markets, which will showcase the relevant Indian Tourism products and 
offerings and B2B meetings. 
 
(v) Connect with Indian Diaspora 

57  
Missions will leverage their connect with Indian Diaspora to motivate them to  
travel to various Indian Destinations. The Mission will also strategize how can  
the diaspora be leveraged to promote Indian tourism in their host countries. 
 
4.3 Annual Events to be hosted by India 
 
Plans for important events for promotion of Inbound Tourism shall be prepared in  
consultation with Indian Missions and Industry Stakeholders. Some of the key 
events are International Buddhist Conclave, India Tourism Mart, Yoga Day etc. 
 
4.4 Annual International Events where India participates 
 
Plans for Important International Travel Marts such as WTM, ITB, ATM etc., which  
help in promoting Inbound tourism shall be prepared in consultation with Indian  
Missions and Industry Stakeholders. Indian Missions shall extend their fullest 
support to Indian delegation including businesses for successful participation. 
 
4.5 Specific Strategy for Medical and Wellness Tourism 
 
Medical tourism, especially wellness tourism and AYUSH may be promoted to 
position India as a health and wellness destination. A coherent strategy to be 
developed by Ministries of Tourism, Culture, AYUSH and External Affairs with Indian  
Missions playing a proactive role in promoting Medical and Wellness Tourism in the  
identified source markets. 
 
4.6 Specific Strategy for MICE Tourism 
 
MICE Tourism (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, Exhibitions) constitutes an 
important element of tourism and has a multiplier effect on the economy. A specific  
strategy to promote India’s MICE offerings and winning bids for international events  
need to planned. Support from the Indian Missions will be crucial for winning the 
bids for hosting the events in India. 
 
4.7 Facilitating VISA 
 
Indian Missions can facilitate VISA for travel and tour operators and other visitors  
such as medical travellers and those attending MICE events in India. Ministry of  
Home Affairs is developing e-VISA mobile application, which can be expedited. 
 
4.8 Facilitating direct connectivity 
 
The Missions can facilitate introduction of direct connectivity from source markets.  
South East Asia, Eastern Europe and South America have huge potential for 
increasing foreign tourist arrivals to India. Therefore, it is important to introduce 

58  
direct flight connectivity from these markets which have a keen interest in India and  
have the potential to contribute to tourist traffic to India.  MoCA may look into  
initiating direct flights between India and countries that are witnessing a rise in the  
number outbound international tourists. 
 
5. Key Operational Areas 
 
5.1 Planning and monitoring of tourism trends 
 
The Missions and India Tourism overseas offices in their resp ective countries will  
carry out the following activities 
(i) Create a database, for the respective country, of travel agencies, tour 
operators, independent travel planners, MICE agencies, travel & consumer 
Media and other relevant stakeholders in the travel industry 
(ii) Monitor relevant tourism trends and opportunities and prepare quarterly 
market reports that can be shared with Ministry of Tourism and the private  
sector stakeholders in the Indian inbound tourism sector 
5.2 Public Relation & Communication 
 
The Missions and India Tourism Overseas offices need to undertake public relation  
and communication relevant to tourism promotion and will carry out the following  
activities 
(i) To track and report articles related to India in the local media 
 
(ii) To ensure placement of positive news stories in trade and consumer media 
 
(iii) To ensure placement of official press releases from MOT 
 
(iv) Image building and to counteract negative publicity as and when required 
 
(v) Active presence on Social Media 
 
5.3 Relationships & Outreach 
 
The Missions and India Tourism Overseas offices will carry out the following activities 
 
(i) To build relationships with various stakeholders to create awareness about  
Indian tourism products 
(ii) To be a source of India related information for the local travel trade, media and 
other stakeholders 

59  
(iii) To engage with museums, universities, trade organizations, local clubs etc. for 
promotion of India 
(iv) To bring annual conferences of travel and hospitality associations in the 
identified markets to India 
(v) To identify eminent opinion makers, celebrities, TV teams, tour operators etc. 
who can be invited to India under the Hospitality scheme of the Ministry 
(vi) To advise in the selection of travel shows for participation 
 
5.4 Support to visiting MOT/ State/ Industry delegations 
 
The Mission to extend necessary support to assist the Ministry of Tourism in 
organizing Road Shows, events, business visits and relevant social events during the  
visit of Ministry officials and/ or cooperating Indian agencies Extend support to State 
Governments/UT Administrations for organizing Road Shows. Inbound tour 
operators travelling from India to various source markets may be provided requisite  
support. 
 
5.5 International Cooperation & Engagement with Multilateral/ Bilateral Forums 
 
Concrete action plans  for Partnerships, learning from experiences of countries that  
have developed strong tourism sectors and collaborating for mutual benefit need to  
be worked out in pursuance of the MOUs signed with different Countries in the field  
of Tourism. 
 
Active engage ment in multilateral forums like UNWTO, G -20, ASEAN, BRICS, IBSA,  
SAARC need to be pursued. Partnerships may be explored with SAARC and ASEAN  
countries to develop and promote common packages on themes that link the 
countries such as the Buddhist circuit, R amayana circuit, Himalayan circuit, Heritage  
circuit that would yield excellent dividends to all participating nations. 
 
5.6 Engagement with international industry bodies 
 
Effective engagement  in close coordination  with Indian industry in international  
industry bodies like the World Travel and Tourism Council (WTTC), Pacific Asia Travel 
Association (PATA) etc. to collaborate with the tourism players across geographies,  
market intelligence, communicate with the global industry on key issues and 
harness their expertise for the benefit of our industry. 
 
5.7 Facilitate FDI into Tourism Sector 

60  
Government of India has allowed 100% FDI in hospitality sector. India is developing  
various destinations and actively promoting investment from Private Sector 
including Public Private Partnerships. The Missions can engage with the trade/ 
industry to promote and encourage investment in tourism and hospitality sector in  
India. 
 
6. Governance and Monitoring 
 
6.1 The Ministry of Tourism will set up a digital platfor m to bring visibility to all the  
stakeholders about the activities to promote Inbound Tourism. It will have a 
dashboard on trends and track performance of Inbound tourism from various 
countries. 
 
6.2 The Ministry of Tourism will organize quarterly meetings with relevant Ministries,  
participating States and Industry Stakeholders to review the progress on various  
initiatives and activities.
